newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 5.

text.p: Privacy commissioner Bruce Slane says data matching by the Social Welfare Department is unreliable and possibly illegal, and he has begun a review of the practice. The department matches its data with that of the Inland Revenue, Customs, and Corrections Departments, the Education Ministry and employers to detect benefit fraud or overpayments. Page 1.

The first sitting of the inaugural MMP parliament could be delayed by two days till Thursday, December 12, to allow NZ First more time to choose a coalition partner. Officially it is still due to sit on Tuesday, December 10, but it is understood that caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger could delay that till Thursday to give NZ First time to conclude final coalition arrangements with either Labour or National. NZ First negotiators said on Wednesday they were still working toward settling an agreement by the time parliament sits. Page 2.

Lost volume in the Australian light beer market has prompted Lion Nathan to give top priority to improving performance to stop further sliding in Australian beer market share. Chief executive Doug Myers told the annual meeting in Auckland on Wednesday that in the year to August the Australian beer market share was 42 percent. But there had been a further decline in the first quarter of the new financial year to 41.2 percent (on a moving annual total basis). Because 68 percent of Lion's business was in Australia, the slump was of major concern. Myers said Lion had the financial capacity to reverse the trend of market share in Australia. Page 15.

A confidential cable services programming agreement between Sky Television and Telecom was revealed on Wednesday as the heart of the Clear Communications claim of conspiracy and anti-competitive behaviour. Clear is trying to get Telecom barred from entering pay televison, Internet services, and other "convergence" markets. Page 15.

Exporters must focus on the real cause of their problems rather than opting for simplistic solutions, the Council of Trade Union says. In a discussion paper sent to all exporters' representatives taking part in an economic summit meeting on Thursday, it says rather than just cutting government spending and lowering wages, exporters would be better off looking at softening monetary policy and improving industry training. Page 15.

Banks were struggling to come to terms with the issues raised by new smartcard technology and have yet to commit to competing brands in the market, Visa International representatives said in Wellington on Wednesday. Page 16.

Requiring companies to specify the maximum price they will offer to buy back their shares will push the market price to that range, Telecom has told the Stock Exchange. The Stock Exchange is inviting submissions on its listing rules relating to share buybacks. Page 16.
